skill.name: consent-registry
skill.description: Use when teams need to record subscriber opt-in, lawful basis, double-opt-in proof, unsubscribe, bounce, complaint, or suppression history. The skill maintains consent records, reconciles import candidates, and routes send approval or suppression work to the correct email skills.
skill.summary: Maintains durable email consent and suppression records.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms one contextual risk: line 67 documents an optional live Resend connector command that can mutate an external ESP roster. The remaining static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, repository-relative links, homepage metadata, and documentation wording. No prompt-injection attempt or data-exfiltration instruction was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Optional live Resend suppression sync can change an external ESP contact roster.
remediation.suggestion: Document a dry-run-first workflow and require explicit user confirmation immediately before any command using --live.

content.value_statement: Email teams need a clear record of opt-ins, opt-outs, complaints, and lawful basis. This skill creates a durable consent registry and routes send decisions to the right auditor.
actual_capabilities: Records subscriber consent status, opt-in timestamp, lawful basis, acquisition source, and double-opt-in proof.
Appends unsubscribe, hard-bounce, spam-complaint, and re-subscribe events with dates and sources.
Reconciles pending consent candidates from imports or ESP suppression exports.
Promotes missing-basis and suppression pointers to the project memory files used by related skills.
Routes send approval, suppression segment work, and deliverability checks to the correct downstream skills.
limitations: It does not provide legal advice or decide whether a campaign may be sent.
It does not build or apply suppression segments in an ESP.
It depends on user-provided records, exports, or pasted evidence.
Optional Resend syncing requires connector setup and explicit live execution.

use_cases.title: Record new opt-ins
use_cases.description: Create a consent record with lawful basis, source, timestamp, and double-opt-in proof before a subscriber enters a list.

use_cases.title: Reconcile suppression exports
use_cases.description: Append unsubscribe, bounce, and complaint events from an ESP export while preserving a dated event history.

use_cases.title: Prepare consent evidence for audit
use_cases.description: Answer what consent facts exist for a subject and identify missing lawful-basis evidence without issuing a send verdict.

prompt_templates.title: Record a simple opt-in
prompt_templates.prompt: Record opt-in for jane@example.com. Source: newsletter form. Date: 2026-06-14. Lawful basis: consent. Double-opt-in confirmed.

prompt_templates.title: Log suppression events
prompt_templates.scenario: Update existing subjects from an ESP export
prompt_templates.prompt: Log these unsubscribe, hard-bounce, and spam-complaint events from our ESP export. Preserve dates, sources, and prior history.

prompt_templates.title: Reconcile candidate records
prompt_templates.prompt: Reconcile the consent candidates from memory/consent/candidates.md. Merge confirmed matches, flag missing lawful basis, and report open identity conflicts.

prompt_templates.title: Review consent evidence before audit
prompt_templates.prompt: For this launch list, summarize each subject consent status, opt-in date, lawful basis, suppression history, and records that need email-quality-auditor review.

output_examples.input: Record opt-in for jane@example.com from a newsletter form with double-opt-in proof.
output: Consent record created for the normalized subscriber identifier.
Status is subscribed with consent basis, source, timestamp, and double-opt-in proof recorded.
No suppression or missing-basis open loops were found.

output_examples.input: Log the latest unsubscribe and complaint export from the ESP.
output: Two unsubscribe events and one complaint event were appended with dates and export source.
Affected subjects were marked unsubscribed or suppressed as appropriate.
Suppression pointers were prepared for the next list-segment-builder step.

output_examples.input: Can we email this imported list?
output_examples.output: The registry can report consent facts and missing records, but it will not approve the send. Use email-quality-auditor for S2 and N1 judgment after records are reconciled.

best_practices: Record the source and date for every consent fact or suppression event.
Use normalized or hashed identifiers and avoid storing marketing profile data.
Route send approval and suppression execution to the dedicated downstream skills.
anti_patterns: Treating a purchased list claim as verified consent without source proof.
Overwriting unsubscribe or complaint history instead of appending dated events.
Using the registry as a campaign approval gate or legal opinion.

faq.question: Does this skill decide if an email send is allowed?
faq.answer: No. It records facts. Use email-quality-auditor for S2 and N1 judgments before a send.

faq.question: Can it handle unsubscribes and spam complaints?
faq.answer: Yes. It appends dated unsubscribe, hard-bounce, complaint, and re-subscribe events with their sources.

faq.question: Does it require an ESP API?
faq.answer: No. Tier 1 use works with pasted records or manual exports. Connector sync is optional.

faq.question: What happens when lawful basis is missing?
faq.answer: The subject is marked as none-on-file and surfaced as an open loop for review.

faq.question: Can it build suppression segments?
faq.answer: No. It records suppression facts. Use list-segment-builder to apply exclusions.

faq.question: How should sensitive identifiers be stored?
faq.answer: Use normalized or hashed identifiers and store only the consent facts needed for audit and operations.
